summary: Machined aluminium 6061-T6 L-bracket. Its horizontal base leg bolts to an undrilled horizontal flat plate with four M6 bolts. Its vertical upright leg carries a 2 kg sensor box on two M5 bolts. The M5 holes are 40 mm apart horizontally, with centres 35 mm above the plate; IMG-01 matches this. The centre of mass is 40 mm from the mounting face. Design factors: dynamic factor 3 and safety factor 2 on yield. The bracket must fit inside an 80 mm cube. All required inputs are covered by the user's answers and the image. The remaining gaps are minor and handled as assumptions, so no new questions are needed.

missing_information.topic: Centre-of-mass position in the plane of the upright face
missing_information.why_it_matters: Only the offset from the mounting face is given (R09). The lateral and vertical position of the centre of mass changes the bending and bolt loads slightly, but the moment arm normal to the face, which governs the design, is known.

missing_information.topic: Clearance holes or tapped holes in the bracket
missing_information.why_it_matters: Determines the hole diameters and the minimum leg thickness. It does not change the interface positions.

assumptions.text: Scope: concept-level design with nominal geometry, checked by hand-calculation (no FEA). No claim of structural safety, regulatory compliance or production readiness.
assumptions.rationale: This is a Prototype 1 bench component; the agent workflow verifies geometry and simple checks only.
assumptions.impact: Results are indicative and need engineering review before use.

assumptions.text: The sensor box centre of mass lies laterally midway between the two M5 holes, at the height of the hole centres, offset 40 mm from the mounting face as stated in R09.
assumptions.rationale: No in-plane position was given. A symmetric mass centred on the bolt pattern is the natural nominal case.
assumptions.impact: An asymmetric centre of mass would add a small torsional or uneven bolt load. The main bending moment is unchanged.

assumptions.text: All bracket holes are through clearance holes. The M5 and M6 bolts are secured with nuts, or with threads in the mating part, not tapped into the bracket.
assumptions.rationale: This is the simplest machined option and is consistent with the plate being drilled to suit (R11).
assumptions.impact: Sets the hole diameters. Tapped holes would need a re-check of the leg thickness.

assumptions.text: The four M6 base bolts are arranged symmetrically in the base leg, inside the 80 mm envelope. The pattern is chosen by the design plan and given to the user for drilling the plate.
assumptions.rationale: The user allowed the plate to be drilled to suit the bracket (R11).
assumptions.impact: The base hole pattern is a design output, not a fixed interface.
